items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The group started out with Basie, Gus Johnson on drums, Jimmie Lewis, who is a bass violin player that we had run into in Louisville, Kentucky, and Freddie Green, of course, guitar. In the front line was me, Buddy DeFranco, and a saxophone player.

ctx.x: . . . a bigger part of the fee.

They wanted to get Basie out of debt, so they put a small band around him, paid him a small salary. As a matter of fact, Buddy DeFranco, the clarinet player – caucasian cat. You know who he is – he was making more money than Basie was, and they put him in Basie’s band. items.title: 68097_Freddie Green oral history interview
items.q: And Clark Terry. And, Marshall, and myself.

ctx.x: And Clark Terry. And, Marshall, and myself. Wasn't Marshall there during that period with Charles?
Not according to this. The earliest with Marshall -- they've got a big band date here with Marshall in it.

items.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995
items.q: But that night on the gig, Freddie, I walked in and you know, Pep would look at you like this, he didn’t even say hello.

ctx.x: At the Brass Rail, right, yeah. So Duke finally he comes around and he says “yeah, I’d like to discuss things with you.” So he says, “okay.” He says, “but we can’t do it out in public, so later on I’ll have to come to your hotel.” So I says, “okay, I’m at the Southway.” He says, “all right, I’ll come by and I’ll call you when I get in the lobby and I’ll hurriedly get out of the lobby and meet you in your room.” So I says, “okay.” So he comes to the hotel, and he calls up and I says, “oh, all right.” So he says,…
